item.title: Strong dollar, weak hand for Trump before midterms
item.description: With the US midterm elections weeks away, a surging dollar is exposing a central contradiction in President Donald Trump's economic agenda: currency markets are delivering the opposite of what his administration wants.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: With the US midterm elections weeks away, a surging dollar is exposing a central contradiction in President Donald Trump's economic agenda: currency markets are delivering the opposite of what his administration wants. Trump's economic record in the first two years of his second term is being heavily scrutinized. Polls show voters' approval of his handling of the economy has rarely been lower. That goes a long way toward explaining why [USN:L4N45Y17K TEXT:"betting markets "]point to his Republican Party losing control of the House of Representatives, and perhaps even the Senate, on November 3. Yet if there's any truth to the market adage that a country's currency is a reflection of the world's confidence in its economy, Trump should be going into the upcoming vote brimming with confidence. The dollar (.DXY) has been rising steadily, recently hitting its [USN:L4N46001K TEXT:"strongest level in 18 months"] against major peers. But a strong and appreciating exchange rate is the last thing Trump wants. His administration's economic and trade policies are aiming to revive US manufacturing, make American exports great again and shrink the trade deficit. A strengthening currency won't help with any of that. WRONG DIRECTION One might expect the dollar to be under pressure, especially given that the [USN:L1N45R0RR TEXT:"US trade balance"] has not narrowed according to the administration's plan. Imports have exploded to record levels, largely driven by US companies hoovering up the chips, equipment and goods needed for the AI build-out , and the country's trade deficit is widening. It was [USN:L1N45F0L5 TEXT:"2.7% of gross domestic product"] earlier this year — one of the smallest readings of the century — but it could be headed for 4% of GDP next year, according to Dean Maki at hedge fund Point72. But the dollar is not weakening. It did during Trump's first year back in the Oval Office, amid concerns about [USN:L1N44H0RB TEXT:""dollar debasement""] and a "sell America" mentality among foreign investors fostered by Trump's tariffs , but that has since gone into reverse. Why? Because exchange rates are relative, and the greenback currently appears to be the proverbial "cleanest dirty shirt." While the US is suffering from acute debt and deficit concerns, so are other developed countries, most [USN:S8N50E09F TEXT:"notably France"]. Investors fear that Paris is unwilling to take the politically unpalatable steps to get its budget under control and are thus slamming the euro . Similarly, worries that higher interest rates will make it nearly impossible for Japan to service its [USN:SPN45900X TEXT:"enormous debt load"] have anchored the yen near its recent historical lows. In short, the dollar is "winning" as much by default as it is benefiting from the flood of global capital chasing the US AI dream. This is not what the White House had in mind. Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent clearly [USN:L8N3YR24M TEXT:"want a weaker dollar"], even if decades of a quasi-official "strong dollar" policy at the White House — dating back to the days of former Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin in the 1990s — make it challenging for them to say so outright. The Trump administration's views on the US currency were flagged almost exactly two years ago in "A User’s Guide to Restructuring the Global Trading System," a paper by Stephen Miran, then a senior strategist at hedge fund Hudson Bay Capital Management. Miran went on to serve as chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers under Trump, who later appointed him as a Federal Reserve governor for a short spell. He has since returned to HBC, but his 41-page manual still appears to serve as a broad framework for the administration's trade, currency and economic policy. The blueprint has come to be known as the "Mar-a-Lago Accord," in a nod to the famous 1985 "Plaza Accord," under which the world's leading economic powers agreed to devalue the dollar. Echoing Trump's decades-long view, Miran wrote that "deep unhappiness with the prevailing economic order is rooted in persistent overvaluation of the dollar ... (which) makes US exports less competitive, US imports cheaper, and handicaps American manufacturing." He has a point. At the time of Trump's inauguration in January last year, the dollar's broad, real effective exchange rate was the strongest in over 30 years. Miran argues that the global trade and financial systems can be rewired to America's benefit, but the path "is narrow, and will require careful planning, precise execution, and attention to steps to minimize adverse consequences." Americans casting their midterm election votes on November 3 may not have the patience for this. While the US economy continues to grow at a healthy pace and unemployment remains low, households are feeling the adverse economic consequences of Trump's policies over the past two years. Tariffs have raised the cost of imported goods, according to a recent New York Fed study , and the US war with Iran, launched in February, has led to soaring energy costs, most notably record-high diesel prices at the pump. As a consequence, inflation remains elevated, bond yields are the highest in a quarter of a century, and real wages are now falling. Given all this, the big question is whether the American public will give the Trump administration the space to try to turn the dollar's tide. A FAREWELL TO MULTILATERALISM Efforts to reverse the dollar's march higher will be challenging, to put it mildly. History suggests that what's needed is multilateral, globally coordinated action, but that is the antithesis of Trump's "America First" worldview. Piecemeal and bilateral actions, like the Treasury's recent [USN:L4N45304A TEXT:"intervention with Japan"] to support the yen , are likely too small to have any lasting impact. Further interventions cannot be ruled out if the dollar continues to strengthen. For example, when writing about the yen, Stephen Jen, CEO of Eurizon SLJ Asset Management, recently argued that a series of targeted, surprise "mini" interventions could chip away at the dollar without triggering an avalanche of depreciation, helping the Trump administration meet its foreign exchange and wider goals over time. "The Trump Administration ... wants to find ways to guide the dollar lower. This is needed because, in order for the US to attain economic security, it needs to reclaim a certain level of manufacturing self-sufficiency. To do that, a weaker dollar would be necessary. The challenge, of course, is to guide the dollar lower without spooking the capital markets," Jen wrote in May. Much will depend on the frequency and size of such moves. Official action to weaken the dollar against major currencies is rare. Before this year's yen intervention, the last time US and Japanese authorities coordinated to sell dollars against the yen was in 1998. The Fed intervened with the European Central Bank and other authorities to support the euro, but that was back in late 2000, just after the single currency's launch. Since the era of free-floating exchange rates began in the early 1970s, when President Richard Nixon took the US off the gold standard, there have only been two truly global efforts to force a change in the dollar's broad value. Both were in the 1980s: the Plaza Accord in 1985 to lower what was an extremely elevated dollar, and the Louvre Accord in 1987 to essentially take the sting out of Plaza. These accords were products of their time. The dollar is nowhere near as strong as it was back then, and that was an era when multilateral cooperation was still in vogue. As the country looks set to enter the final two years of the Trump era, the dollar's relative strength could say much about how much of his economic agenda he has been able to achieve since first entering the White House almost 10 years ago. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. Follow ROI on LinkedIn, and X. And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple , Spotify , or the Reuters app . item.title: トランプ氏、対ロシア制裁法の適用を発動直前に免除
item.description:
Kanishka Singh Jasper Ward
[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kanishka Singh　Jasper Ward

[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は先月署名した法律に基づくロシア関連の主要な制裁と関税の適用を免除した。ロシア製品への関税や、同国の石油・天然ガスを購入する国への制裁が対象となる。これらは数日後に発効する予定だった。

ホワイトハウスが１６日に公表した大統領令で、トランプ氏は適用免除が米国の国益にかなうと説明した。免除はトランプ氏または政府高官が「追加措置が適切」と判断するまで有効となる。

同法は共和党の故リンゼー・グラム上院議員が推進し、トランプ氏が９月中旬に署名した。ロシア産原油・天然ガスの輸入上位５カ国から米国に輸入される製品に、３０日以内に最大１００％の関税を課す内容となっていた。法律成立から３０日後以降にロシア産と知りながら石油・天然ガスを購入した国や、ロシアの制裁逃れを支援する上位５カ国も対象に含まれていた。

トランプ氏は大統領令で「現時点でこうした適用免除を行うことが米国の国益にかなうとする証明書を議会に提出した」と述べた。同法では、大統領は制裁が国益にかなわないと判断したと議会に通知するだけで、制裁を免除できる。

バージニア州選出のドン・ベイヤー民主党下院議員は、今回の措置を強く批判した。声明で「トランプ氏は今回もプーチン（ロシア大統領）に屈し、パートナーであるウクライナを再び裏切った。ロシアの違法な侵略戦争を罰するための法律に込められた議会の明確な意思にも背いている」と述べた。

トランプ氏は最近ロシアと結んだ軽油に関する合意でも、一部の共和党議員を含む複数の米上院議員から批判を受けていた。

item.title: Pumas UNAM vence al Atlante en el torneo mexicano con doblete del brasileño Juninho
item.description: Pumas UNAM ganó el viernes 2-1 de visita al Atlante con un doblete del brasileño Juninho en la duodécima jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pumas UNAM ganó el viernes 2-1 de visita al Atlante con un doblete del brasileño Juninho en la duodécima jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano. Con su cuarta victoria en el torneo, el club de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México llegó a 16 puntos y se ubicó en el noveno lugar de la tabla general, cerca de la zona que da acceso a la postemporada. Los primeros ocho lugares al término de las 17 jornadas de la fase regular obtienen ese boleto. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, Pumas se puso en ventaja a los 42 minutos cuando Juninho remató de derecha en el área chica tras un pase de cabeza del paraguayo Robert Morales. Atlante empató en tiempo de reposición de la primera parte con un potente disparo de Luis Calzadilla desde fuera del área, que metió el balón pegado al poste izquierdo. Pumas selló el triunfo a los 72 minutos con el doblete de Juninho, quien cerró una jugada de contragolpe con un potente zurdazo en el área tras recibir un pase del panameño Adalberto Carrasquilla. En los otros partidos del viernes, Atlas ganó 2-0 de visita a Necaxa con goles del belga Ryan Mmaee y del argentino Manuel Capasso. Con su sexto triunfo, los "Rojinegros" del Atlas llegaron a 21 puntos y se ubicaron momentáneamente en el segundo lugar general, por debajo de América que registra las mismas unidades, pero una mejor diferencia de gol. Por su parte, Tijuana y Puebla empataron 0-0. La actividad continuará el sábado cuando Santos Laguna enfrente a Querétaro, Guadalajara juegue como local ante Tigres UANL, América visite a León, Toluca reciba al Atlético de San Luis y el vigente campeón Cruz Azul enfrente a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez. La jornada concluirá el domingo cuando Monterrey reciba a Pachuca.

item.title: Magnitude 5.6 earthquake strikes Pakistan's Balochistan province, GFZ says
item.description: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck near Khuzdar in Pakistan's Balochistan province on Saturday, the German Research Center for Geosciences (GFZ) said. The quake was at a depth of 10 km (6 miles), GFZ
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck near Khuzdar in Pakistan's Balochistan province on Saturday, the German Research Center for Geosciences (GFZ) said. The quake was at a depth of 10 km (6 miles), GFZ said.

item.title: Figueroa loses WBA featherweight title after missing weight
item.description: American Brandon Figueroa has been stripped of his WBA featherweight title after hitting the scales 1.4 pounds over the 126-pound weight limit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: American Brandon Figueroa has been stripped of his WBA featherweight title after hitting the scales 1.4 pounds over the 126-pound weight limit for Saturday's fight against Tomoki Kameda of Japan, organisers said on Friday. Kameda, 35, will be able to clinch the vacant title if he wins the fight, which will go ahead as scheduled in Las Vegas. "Honestly, it's disrespectful, because I'm here, I suffered too. I did my thing. I'm ready for tomorrow," Kameda said, speaking via a translator. "It has been 18 months since I fought, but look at me, look how shredded I am. You know I'm ready. Everything remains the same, I'm going for the title tomorrow." Figueroa, 29, clinched the featherweight title in February after beating Briton Nick Ball in Liverpool. If he wins the fight against Kameda, the title will remain vacant.

item.title: IMFC chair says global economy resilient; delegates walk out on Russian official
item.description: A US official said Washington supports Russia's presence despite European concerns.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, David Lawder, Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: The global economy is showing great resilience but there is no room for complacency, the head of the International Monetary Fund's steering committee said on Saturday, while divisions over Russia's war against Ukraine sparked a walkout of delegates. Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan, who heads the IMF's steering committee, asked about the walkout by nearly half of delegates during remarks by Russia's finance minister at a meeting on Saturday, said the important thing was that members ultimately agreed to the chair's statement. "We came here for a reason, and we achieved it. Look at this chair statement, it clearly says that all members agreed to the statement, so that's what matters," the chair of the International Monetary and Financial Committee told Reuters. Al-Jadaan told a press conference that the global economy was demonstrating "[USN:L1N463024 TEXT:"remarkable resilience"]" in the face of profound ongoing challenges, including wars, threats to energy and food security, high public debt levels, and risks linked to the rapid development of artificial intelligence, while warning finance officials against letting down their guard. "The message from the IMFC members is clear: There is no room for complacency," Al-Jadaan said in the final press conference of a week of IMF and World Bank annual meetings that brought more than 18,000 people to Bangkok. Fiscal authorities should work to rebuild buffers while protecting vulnerable populations and growth-enhancing investments, Al-Jadaan told reporters, underscoring the need for continued central bank independence and policies that supported private sector-led growth and investment. He said IMFC members called for increasing support to countries that are facing short-term financing challenges caused by spillovers from wars and high energy prices. "International cooperation remains critical to addressing excessive global imbalances and trade tensions," he said. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva called the meetings productive but said there was clearly heightened anxiety among members about increasing divergence. Many lower income countries that were not part of the AI-value chain feared they were falling behind, she said. "These meetings also have shown that in a world of repetitive shocks and geopolitical fragmentation, still there is desire for multilateral dialogue and cooperation," she said. The Development Committee, which groups the boards of both the World Bank and the IMF, touched on similar themes in its statement, underscoring the urgent need to end wars and conflicts to ensure sustainable growth and long-term stability. "Our priority remains to promote macroeconomic and financial stability while enabling broad-based, private sector-led growth, and strengthening resilience through credible policies and international cooperation," the committee's chair, Swedish Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson, said. WALKOUT AMID TENSIONS Those comments came shortly after many IMFC delegates left the room when Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov addressed the group in Russian. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel told a bank event on the sidelines of the meetings that nearly 50% of delegates took part in the walkout, sending a clear message to Russia. "This is a very strong signal about solidarity and values. It would be the best for the world economy if this unprovoked war of aggression against Ukraine would end," Nagel said. "I was really proud so many left this plenary." Ukraine's central bank chief, Andriy Pyshnyi, told Reuters he was surprised by the large number of finance officials who left the room, calling it a [USN:L1N46303F TEXT:""deep and emotional moment.""] The Bank of England confirmed that Governor Andrew Bailey was among the delegates who joined the walkout, which comes ahead of Britain hosting the G20 next year. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, who may be in the frame to take over as [USN:L6N4610XU TEXT:"chair of the World Economic Forum"], stayed in the room, two people in the meeting said. Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has roiled the IMFC, preventing it from reaching consensus statements in the years since. There were deep divisions again this week as [USN:L1N46209U TEXT:"tensions flared between the US and Ukraine"]. People in the meeting said those who left while Siluanov spoke included delegates from Britain, Germany, France, Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, among others. "The Ukraine war is existential for us in Europe," one European diplomat said. "We cannot normalize relations with Russia." Germany on Thursday warned against efforts to [USN:L1N4610HQ TEXT:"bring Russia back"] on to the international stage after Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers, just over a month after the US hosted his first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine, at a meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. US Treasury Under Secretary Erin Browne told Reuters the same day that Washington, the current leader of the G20, supported Russia's presence. "We think it's really important if you're going to solve a crisis, you need to have open dialogue and open conversation," she told Reuters. "And you can't have ... dialogue, and you can't have resolution to conflict if no one's talking to one another." Ukraine's finance minister participated virtually in the meetings, in order to focus on budget priorities at home. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, speaking at a European Union summit on Friday, blasted US President Donald Trump's recent [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"diesel deal"] with Russia. EU leaders have rallied around Zelenskiy after Trump again criticised Ukraine and called its strikes on Russian refineries a "disgrace." Trump on Friday [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"waived"] a new congressional requirement to impose harsh sanctions on Russia.

item.title: German minister seeks debt-brake exemption to sustain Ukraine aid
item.description: Germany's development minister is seeking an exemption from the country's debt brake, a constitutional limit on government borrowing, for Ukraine funding, arguing that much of Germany's civilian support for Ukraine comes from her ministry's budget.
item.dc:creator: Maria Martinez
item.content:encoded: Germany's development minister is seeking an exemption from the country's debt brake, a constitutional limit on government borrowing, for Ukraine funding, arguing that much of Germany's civilian support for Ukraine comes from her ministry's budget. "The Russian attacks are more severe than ever, leading to more deaths, more destruction, more suffering. But as budget cuts for development assistance continue, we simply will not be able to maintain our support for Ukraine at this level," Reem Alabali Radovan told Reuters on Friday, on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings. Funding for Ukraine in her ministry's budget amounts to about €330 million ($371 million) this year, down from €670 million in 2022 and €750 million in 2023. "At this point, it is not a political decision; we just face massive cuts and it will no longer be possible," Alabali Radovan said. "This is especially hard as the money is wisely invested in Ukraine's and Europe's stability." Alabali Radovan is a member of the Social Democrats, the junior partner of the governing coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU. Her proposal has the backing of Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, a member of the conservative CDU, but faces opposition from other members of the party who oppose further exceptions to borrowing rules beyond those already approved, such as for defence spending. "I am already prioritising support for Ukraine, but there are many other crises and conflicts, too. And we work in the long term, which means large parts of our budget are already committed," Alabali Radovan said. "That means the cuts hit crisis instruments above all, because – naturally – they work with flexible funds that are not yet pre-committed." Alabali Radovan added that she supports Merz's call for other countries to contribute more. "We are the strongest supporters, and I believe others can and should contribute more," she said. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
item.description: Authorities reported violent incidents in several cities, including vandalism in Marseille and attacks targeting police, media and public buildings.
item.dc:creator: Stamos Prousalis
item.content:encoded: Clashes broke out between police and protesters in cities across France on Saturday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets in some of the country's most violent protests in years over rising costs and declining public services. Some 272 people had been arrested by mid-afternoon after violent incidents involving hooded individuals, including in Paris, Marseille in the south, Rennes in the northwest, Toulouse in the southwest and Angers in the west, the Interior Ministry said. "Such actions include attempted looting, confrontations with law enforcement, the setting of fires to street furniture and the targeting of seats of power and media outlets," it said, blaming the unrest on what it described as the "ultra-left". In Lyon, in east-central France, protesters also set ablaze a tourist office. The protests began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards. "We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris. A large police presence was visible in central Paris, especially near landmarks such as the Champs-Elysees and the Arc de Triomphe, which were excluded from the routes of two authorised demonstrations. Protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked President Emmanuel Macron's previous term in office. In Marseille, the mayor said the town hall had been vandalised and that additional police were being sent to the city following talks with the prime minister and interior minister. About 100 people walked towards the start of the protests shouting "All cops are bastards", according to a Reuters witness. Macron, who urged calm on Friday, is entering [USN:L1N45Y033 TEXT:"the final stretch"] of his presidency amid a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy. France's efforts to reduce public debt have failed to reassure investors, pushing government [USN:L8N45R0RA TEXT:"borrowing costs"] to their highest levels in more than two decades. POLICE RESPONSE UNDER SCRUTINY Police tactics have drawn criticism following a series of [USN:L6N45V0HM TEXT:"injuries"] among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand after picking up a stun grenade. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said more than 900 police officers had also been injured in previous protests. The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence. France suspended the use of stun grenades during the student demonstrations, but Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they could be used on Saturday. Calls on social media for veterans of previous protest movements to join the demonstrations appeared to have broadened participation, raising the prospect of larger. The Yellow Vest movement emerged in 2018 in opposition to diesel taxes before expanding into a wider protest against living costs and inequality. The movement subsided after Macron announced billions of euros in tax cuts. Yannick Maillou, a teacher from La Crèche in western France who participated in the Yellow Vest movement, said several gathering points had been organised locally for Saturday's protests, with labour unions also encouraging participation.

item.title: Could Trump interfere in the midterms? | On Assignment
item.description: Reporters lay out scenarios where Trump could try to sway election results.
item.content:encoded:
Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app.

As President Donald Trump seeks greater influence over how elections are run, election officials across the country are bracing for disputes over voting, ballot counting and the certification of results. Reuters reporters Peter Eisler and Mike Spector join On Assignment to discuss the scenarios officials and legal experts fear could test the boundaries of federal authority before and after the 2026 midterms. item.title: Mongolia becomes new donor to World Bank's fund for poorest countries
item.description: The World Bank Group said on Saturday that Mongolia has become a new donor to the International Development Association fund for the poorest countries, after previously spending nearly three decades as a recipient of IDA funding.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The World Bank Group said on Saturday that Mongolia has become a new donor to the International Development Association fund for the poorest countries, after previously spending nearly three decades as a recipient of IDA funding. The development lender said that Mongolia's parliament approved a 4.8 billion tugrik ($1.3 million) contribution to the latest IDA funding round, marking a milestone in the country's development journey. Since becoming a World Bank member country in 1991, Mongolia has received more than $1.62 billion in development financing, including IDA support for transport, rural development, health and education. Mongolia graduated from IDA support in July 2020, becoming a client of the World Bank's main lending arm for middle-income countries, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. "Mongolia’s contribution to IDA21 marks an important milestone in our longstanding partnership with the World Bank and reflects our commitment to international solidarity," Mongolian Finance Minister Mendsaikhan Zagdjav said in a statement released by the World Bank. "Having benefited firsthand from IDA’s support, we recognize the vital role of concessional financing in helping countries reduce poverty, build resilience, and expand opportunities. As we continue to advance Mongolia's own development priorities, we are proud to support other countries in pursuing theirs."

item.title: Bruins escape 2-goal hole, emerge with win over Ducks
item.description: Elias Lindholm scored to break a third-period tie, capping a two-point performance as the visiting Boston Bruins registered a come-from-behind 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Elias Lindholm scored to break a third-period tie, capping a two-point performance as the visiting Boston Bruins registered a come-from-behind 4-2 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Friday. David Pastrnak netted one goal and one assist for the Bruins, who scored four unanswered goals, three on the power play, to run their winning streak to four games. Frederic Brunet potted his first career NHL goal, Matthew Poitras added a tally, and Pavel Zacha and James Hagens each logged two assists. Bruins goaltender Michael DiPietro made 25 saves to earn his first NHL victory in his sixth game and fourth start. Tim Washe and Beckett Sennecke scored for the Ducks, who squandered a 2-0 lead and have dropped their second game in a row. Goalie Lukas Dostal stopped 18 shots. While the Bruins converted three of their four power-play opportunities, the Ducks were blanked on five chances with the extra skater. Anaheim also mustered only four shots on goal in the third period. After watching his team erase a 2-0 deficit, Lindholm put Boston on top at 8:18 of the third period with a tap-in tally set up by Zacha while on a power play. Poitras added an insurance goal eight minutes later when he finished a 2-on-1 rush on a setup from Hagens. Anaheim tallied twice late in the first period. Washe opened the scoring with 37.3 seconds remaining in the frame, finding the twine with his long shot from the point that made it through a screen and DiPietro's legs. Sennecke doubled the lead 21 seconds later, notching his fifth of the season by finishing a three-way passing play. Brunet, a 2022 fifth-round draft choice, halved Boston's deficit at 3:15 of the second period. He sent a long shot from the blue line that made it through the maze of traffic for his milestone marker. Pastrnak tied the clash with another man-advantage goal at 3:26 of the third period, pouncing on a loose puck during a scramble for his third of the campaign. Pastrnak took sole possession of the fourth spot on the Bruins' all-time goals list with his 423rd career tally, passing Brad Marchand. He trails only Johnny Bucyk (545 goals), Phil Esposito (459) and Patrice Bergeron (427). --Field Level Media

item.title: BOJ may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast, IMF says
item.description: The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan is "doing the right thing" by normalising monetary policy and may need to raise interest rates faster if inflation rises more than expected, a senior International Monetary Fund official told Reuters. Japan must also clarify how it plans to fund its big spending plans and lay out a medium-term fiscal framework to ease market concerns about fiscal risks, said Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department. "I would say that they are doing the right thing at this point," Srinivasan said on the BOJ's efforts to lift its policy rate towards levels deemed neutral to the economy. "If inflation rises faster than expected, you have to start tightening faster because you don't want inflation expectations to get un-anchored. It's data dependent," he said in an interview on Friday. The remarks came ahead of the BOJ's key policy meeting later this month, when it [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"could keep rates steady"] but drop hawkish hints that would reinforce dominant market expectations of a December hike. Inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and brisk AI-demand were among key themes discussed by policymakers gathering for this week's annual IMF meetings in Bangkok. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, who attended the IMF meetings, said on [USN:L1N4620G5 TEXT:"Friday"] the central bank will focus on anchoring underlying inflation around its 2% target and won't tolerate any overshoot, stressing anew its resolve to continue raising interest rates. For Japan, a weak yen adds to factors pushing up inflation by boosting the cost of raw material imports. Such mounting price pressures prodded the BOJ to raise rates to a 31-year high of 1.25% in [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"September"], following a hike in June. Many analysts expect another rate increase by year-end. Japan also conducted a rare, coordinated intervention with the US on [USN:L1N43Z05E TEXT:"July 31"] to prevent the currency's slide to near 40-year lows from destabilising financial markets. In staff analysis included in its report on Asia's economy, the IMF said a big portion of yen moves since mid-2025 had little to do with fundamental factors such as yield differentials, and instead co-moved with speculative positions in yen futures. "Japan has a deep foreign exchange market, so as a first line of defense, they have allowed the exchange rate to move," Srinivasan said. "Bottom line, I would say that the Japanese authorities are fully committed to a freely floating exchange rate. I've had many discussions with them. So I don't doubt that at all," he said when asked if the recent yen intervention was justified. FISCAL FRAMEWORK NEEDED Rising global bond yields have also drawn attention at this week's IMF meetings as debt in advanced economies, including Japan, expanded after years of heavy spending. Markets worry that Japan may add to its already huge debt pile with the administration's big spending plans and a two-year cut to the consumption tax from April next year. Srinivasan said Japan has in fact seen fiscal consolidation proceed more than any other G7 country since the pandemic due in part to rising tax revenues. "Markets are concerned about the fiscal risks because of the uncertainty" on how Japan would pay for the fresh spending and tax-cut plans, he said. "Japan also would benefit from having a medium-term fiscal framework."

item.title: Major development banks step up support for critical minerals value chains
item.description: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) will strengthen efforts to help mineral-rich developing economies add more value to their resources by moving beyond extraction into processing, refining and manufacturing, according to an outline of a critical minerals collaboration framework published on Saturday. The banks involved include the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank, according to the outline The October framework calls for coordinated support across critical mineral supply chains, including financing, infrastructure and policy aimed at creating jobs, boosting domestic value addition, attracting private investment and supporting low-carbon transition MDBs plan to support mineral corridors incorporating power, transport, logistics, water and digital infrastructure, while strengthening project preparation and using co-financing, guarantees and other financing tools to mobilise capital and accelerate private sector investments They will also seek closer alignment on environmental and social standards, coordinate support to governments and better connect mining projects with infrastructure and industrial development An MDB working group will coordinate implementation of the framework's objectives and report annually to the Heads of MDBs Group on progress

item.title: Canada women snap world champion England's 41-match unbeaten run
item.description: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday, achieving a goal they have long been working toward.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Fernandes
item.content:encoded: Canada’s women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday, achieving a goal they have long been working toward. One month after halting England's 39-match winning streak following a 26-26 draw in Exeter, a late try from Shoshanah Seumanutafa put Canada ahead with less than three minutes left to play. “Definitely special," Canada captain Sophie de Goede told reporters after the landmark win. "I think there were a lot of ups and downs throughout that game and we really had to grind it out and find a way, and that's kind of the DNA of our team and our group. "So, I think more than anything, I feel proud of the way that we found a way to win that game, and it wasn't easy.” The opener of a two-game Rugby Rematch Tour between the growing rivals drew an electric crowd to BMO Field as Canada returned to home soil for the first time since finishing runner-up to the Red Roses at last year's World Cup. "I think it's a little bit more than just the score at the end because we won on so many levels today," Canada's Justine Pelletier said. "Off the field, just the crowd, being home, and there's so much going on around. And I think that win at the end on the pitch was just the cherry on (top)." Savannah Bauder, Alysha Corrigan and DaLeaka Menin also scored tries for Canada, while Maddie Feaunati, Zoe Harrison and Sarah Bern added one each for England. England's unbeaten run had stretched back to their World Cup final defeat by New Zealand in 2022. Canada’s last win over the Red Roses came in 2016 at the Women's Rugby Super Series. “It was good to beat England, but I think for a few years now we knew that we could beat them," Pelletier said. "It was just a matter of time and a matter of putting every detail together." For top-ranked England, having a target on their back is nothing new. “The bit we always remember is we're at the top, and when you're at the top, people want to bring you down as quick as they can,” England captain Megan Jones said, adding that the team take "huge pride" in their unbeaten run. Jones also praised the atmosphere in Toronto, where 18,621 fans rocked the stands all night in chilly conditions, setting an attendance record for a women’s rugby match in North America. "We're the biggest advocates for the game," Jones said of players. "So we're always going to try and grow the game as much as we can, and Canada definitely did that in tenfold today." Canada and England will face off in the second game of the Rugby Rematch Tour on October 23 in Ottawa.

item.title: Nathan MacKinnon’s 4-point night powers Avalanche past Penguins
item.description: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday in Denver.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists to lead the Colorado Avalanche to a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday in Denver. Artturi Lehkonen scored twice while Gabriel Landeskog and T.J. Hughes added goals for the Avalanche, who went 2-0-1 while playing three games in four nights. Martin Necas had three assists, Cale Makar added two, and Mackenzie Blackwood made 29 saves. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust got the goals for the Penguins, who are 1-4-1 in their past six. Arturs Silovs turned away 27 shots. Colorado scored the only three goals of the second period to go up 4-2. Lehkonen notched his second goal of the night 25 seconds into the frame, tying it 2-2. He knocked down the rebound of MacKinnon's shot off the goalpost with his glove and scored from the crease. Landeskog gave Colorado the lead for good at 4:24, slamming a Brock Nelson pass into the open side of the net. Hughes scored his first career NHL goal when he tipped in MacKinnon's pass with 5:03 left in the period, four seconds after an Avalanche power play expired. MacKinnon added a power-play goal on a one-timer from just above the left dot with 4:54 left in the third to make it five straight goals for the Avalanche. He has 16 points (six goals and 10 assists) in eight games this season. Silovs stopped MacKinnon's penalty-shot attempt 15 seconds before Landeskog's goal. Pittsburgh jumped ahead 2-0 with two goals 29 seconds apart in the first period. Malkin scored as he cut across the slot after charging down the right wing. He shot as he fell and beat Blackwood 8:28 into the game. Rust then tipped in Sidney Crosby's pass on a 2-on-1 rush at 8:57. Colorado got on the board at 11:01 of the first when Lehkonen tipped in a pass from MacKinnon off the rush. New Avalanche assistant coach Brett McLean made his debut behind the bench after replacing Dave Hakstol, who departed to become the head coach at Arizona State. --Field Level Media

item.title: Apple appoints Meta veteran Scott Tucker to lead global litigation
item.description: Tucker will oversee commercial and patent litigation worldwide and legal matters involving Apple's financial services as the company faces mounting lawsuits under General Counsel Jennifer Newstead ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mark Gurman Apple Inc. has tapped a longtime Meta Platforms Inc. executive as its new litigation chief, bolstering its legal team at a time when the iPhone maker faces a growing array of lawsuits. The company has hired Scott Tucker, a longtime deputy general counsel and litigation chief at Meta, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The move reunites Tucker with new Apple General Counsel Jennifer Newstead, who is bringing on a trusted lieutenant from her time at the social networking giant. Tucker is becoming Apple’s vice president of global litigation and financial services, a newly created position overseeing commercial and patent litigation worldwide, said the people, who asked not to be named because the move isn’t public. He’ll also manage legal matters involving the company’s financial offerings.  The appointment means Heather Grenier, Apple’s current vice president of commercial and competition litigation, will move one level lower in the organisation, reporting to Tucker instead of directly to Newstead. Grenier will still remain on Newstead’s legal leadership team.  Tucker, in addition to his tenure at Meta, previously held a senior legal position at Morgan Stanley, giving him experience relevant to his new financial services responsibilities. Newstead took over as Apple’s general counsel in March after serving as Meta’s top lawyer for six years. Kyle Andeer, another senior member of Apple’s legal department and its longtime vice president managing regulatory and product-related legal matters, is seeing his role expand. He is gaining oversight of international legal matters and functions involving online child safety, cybersecurity and law enforcement. Spokespeople for Apple and Meta declined to comment.  The changes are part of a broader reorganisation under Newstead, who oversees legal and government affairs. Apple recently hired Nate Gatten, a former American Airlines Group Inc. executive, as its vice president of government affairs. The company has also appointed new government affairs leads for different international regions. Apple combined its legal and government affairs groups under Newstead following the recent retirements of Lisa Jackson, the former head of environmental, policy and social initiatives, and previous top lawyer Kate Adams. Former Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook, now the company’s executive chairman, has also taken a leading role in government affairs. Apple is waging a variety of legal battles, including a sweeping US antitrust lawsuit, its long-running dispute with Epic Games Inc. over App Store restrictions, and litigation related to privacy and delays to Siri features. The company has faced billions of dollars in judgments and settlements in recent years, while regulators in the US and Europe have challenged business practices central to the iPhone maker’s operations. Some Apple executives believe the company hasn’t fared as well in court as it should have, particularly in litigation involving the App Store. Those setbacks have forced Apple to change its commission structure and the circumstances under which it can charge developers. The changes threaten to significantly slow growth in Apple’s services business, a key driver of revenue expansion in recent years. A slowdown in that business would deal a major blow to the company’s overall financial performance. Even in the best of times, overseeing Apple’s litigation is a difficult job. The Cupertino, California-based company is among the most frequently sued businesses in the world, facing cases ranging from slip-and-fall claims at its retail stores to multibillion-dollar antitrust disputes. Grenier took over the role under particularly challenging circumstances, replacing her predecessor just before Apple’s landmark trial against Epic Games began in 2021. Her tenure has also spanned two major leadership transitions: the appointment of John Ternus as CEO and Newstead’s arrival. In recent weeks, Ternus has overseen a sweeping series of executive changes, including the appointment of new leaders for the App Store, events and corporate functions such as information security and real estate. The reshuffling also includes the departure of the longtime Apple Pay chief, the replacement of the company’s mergers and acquisitions head, and a reorganisation of the company’s hardware engineering division.

item.title: Carapaz joins NSN on three-year deal
item.description: Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Former Giro d'Italia winner and Olympic champion Richard Carapaz joined NSN Cycling Team on Friday, after leaving EF Education-EasyPost a year before the end of his contract. The 33-year-old Ecuadorean, who won the Giro in 2019 and road race gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, signed a three-year deal with NSN, formerly known as Israel–Premier Tech. "I'm really looking forward to it, and to be honest, this reminds me a lot of when I signed my first professional contract, when I was incredibly excited about being in the WorldTour," Carapaz said in a statement. "The team has big ambitions to keep growing and already in my conversations with the performance team, it was clear we share the same desire to keep improving and achieve big things together." Carapaz, renowned for his climbing ability, won two stages at this year's Tour de France to finish eighth overall.

item.title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island
item.description: Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory's vulnerable elephant seal population.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory's vulnerable elephant seal population. Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said official testing confirmed the highly pathogenic virus strain "in samples collected from an elephant seal and a kelp gull on Macquarie Island, marking the first H5 event on this island". Australia in June became the last continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected in late 2025 on another of its sub-Antarctic territories, Heard Island, where more than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus, according to local media. Like Heard Island, Macquarie Island, a UNESCO World Heritage-listed territory located in the Southern Ocean halfway between Australia's Tasmania state and Antarctica, is a key breeding ground for southern elephant seals. The mammals, which can weigh up to 3,600 kg (7,936 pounds), are particularly susceptible to H5 bird flu, with pup mortality rates in some cases of more than 90%, according to the federal government. In August, Australia's environment department said it would withdraw personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island due to the "psycho-social risk to expeditioners of a potential H5 avian influenza outbreak". Expert assessments predicted the virus would likely cause a significant elephant seal mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, the environment department said.

item.title: サッカー＝インテル、主将マルティネスが負傷で7試合欠場へ─報道
item.description: ［１６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１６日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイタリア・セリエＡ、インテルの主将ラウタロ・マルティネスがハムストリングの負傷により今後７試合を欠場する見通しとなった。米スポーツ専門局ＥＳＰＮが１６日に伝えた。

マルティネスは１３日にホームで行われた欧州チャンピオンズリーグ（ＣＬ）、３─４で敗れたクラブ・ブルージュ（ベルギー）戦にフル出場し、２得点を記録。しかし、１５日に行った検査の結果、左ハムストリングの肉離れが判明した。

インテルのクリスティアン・キブ監督は１６日、「彼はしばらく離脱することになる。私は医師ではないが、復帰までの目安は聞いている。おそらく代表戦期間明けには戻ってくるだろう」と述べた。

これにより、マルティネスは１７日のボローニャ戦と、２１日のＣＬシャフタル・ドネツク（ウクライナ）戦の欠場が確実となった。１１月の代表戦期間までには、３１日に行われるＡＣミランとのダービーを含め、７試合が予定されている。

マルティネスは今季、公式戦７試合に出場して６得点を記録。昨季はセリエＡで１７ゴールを挙げ、自身２回目となるリーグ得点王に輝いている。

item.title: Juez mexicano condena a 158 años en prisión a asesinos de surfistas extranjeros
item.description: Un juez mexicano condenó el viernes a tres hombres a 158 años y nueve meses de prisión por el asesinato de dos hermanos australianos y de su amigo estadounidense durante un viaje de surf en 2024 al estado de Baja California, informó una fuente judicial.
item.dc:creator: Lizbeth Diaz, Yolanda Morales
item.content:encoded: Un juez mexicano condenó el viernes a tres hombres a 158 años y nueve meses de prisión por el asesinato de dos hermanos australianos y de su amigo estadounidense durante un viaje de surf en 2024 al estado de Baja California, informó una fuente judicial. La semana pasada el mismo juez [USN:L6N45V14R TEXT:" declaro culpables"] a Jesús Gerardo "N" alias "El Kekas", Irineo Francisco "N" y Ángel Jesús "N" de homicidio y robo calificado cuando se cometa de noche, robo con violencia y robo de vehículo con violencia, en agravio de los hermanos Jake y Callum Robinson así como de su amigo Jack Carter Rhoad. Además de la condena, el juez ordenó el pago de una multa de poco más de un millón de pesos como reparación del daño a la familia de los hermanos Robinson, así como de 549 mil pesos a la familia Carter, dijo una fuente del poder Judicial el estado Baja California. “Desde el fondo de mi corazón, agradezco a todas las personas y a todos los testigos”, dijo por Zoom Page Rhoad, madre del joven estadounidense asesinado, al concluir la audiencia a la que Reuters asistió. "Nunca habrá justicia por perder un hijo, pero estos hombres no volverán a hacer daño a nadie mas", agregó. Los cuerpos de los extranjeros fueron encontrados dentro de un pozo de agua con heridas de bala en la cabeza, días después de que su familia reportara su desaparición en abril de 2024. La camioneta en que viajaban fue localizada calcinada en otro punto, a varios kilómetros de donde ocurrieron los hechos. Aunque Ensenada se considera relativamente segura, Baja California se encuentra entre los estados más violentos de México. Tras los asesinatos, el Departamento de Estado estadounidense instó a sus ciudadanos a reconsiderar viajar a la zona debido a los riesgos de delincuencia y secuestro. El 19 de noviembre, Gisell Silva, entonces novia de "El Kekas", fue condenada a 20 años de prisión por su participación en el caso. La mujer de entonces 23 años fue detenida pocos días después de que fueron encontrados los cadáveres de los extranjeros. Martin y Debra Robinson, padres de Jake y Callum, siguieron la audiencia de sentencia de forma remota tras regresar a Australia la semana pasada, luego de conocer el fallo de culpabilidad. Entrevistados al salir de una de las 24 audiencias que duró el proceso, describieron la muerte de sus hijos como “un infierno” y una experiencia “increíblemente difícil”. La lectura final de la sentencia está programada para el 23 de octubre, dijo la misma fuente del Poder Judicial.

item.title: Rainout forces Guardians, Rays to play ALCS straight through to finish
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Major League Baseball officials did not want to postpone Game 4 of the American League Championship Series, but soaking, day-long rain forced their hand.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Major League Baseball officials did not want to postpone Game 4 of the American League Championship Series, but soaking, day-long rain forced their hand. As a result, the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays will play the rescheduled contest on Saturday night. Cleveland leads the best-of-seven series 2-1. Guardians right-hander Shawn Armstrong (0-0, 0.00 ERA postseason) takes on Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (0-0, 4.91 ERA postseason). Both were slated to start Friday before the game was called one hour after its scheduled first pitch, but play never began. "It was obviously a long day to wait to not have a game," said Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt, who was visibly and audibly perturbed at his post-rainout press conference. "It's completely out of our control, but this is what happens. "This is baseball. This is Cleveland. We're more than used to these kinds of days." The postponement will force the teams to play the final four games on consecutive days, if needed, with Game 5 in Cleveland on Sunday. The series would return to St. Petersburg, Fla., for Game 6 and Game 7, if necessary. Since the Rays play in a domed stadium and there is no rain in the forecast for Northeast Ohio this weekend, the AL crown will be awarded no later than Tuesday. Temperatures for the next two games are expected to be in the low 40s. "No, I'm not frustrated at all," Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said. "I have no reason to be frustrated. We did everything just like we would do during the regular season. There was no guarantee there wasn't another band of rain coming." Armstrong, a former Rays reliever, allowed one hit over 1 2/3 scoreless innings in Game 2. He will serve as the opener, with left-hander Joey Cantillo and right-hander Slade Cecconi likely among those to follow. Armstrong was less fortunate in his previous outing against Tampa Bay, allowing three runs in two-thirds of an inning in a no-decision on July 24. He has a 6.14 ERA in 16 total appearances against the Rays (regular season and postseason), all out of the bullpen. "If you compare both organizations on paper and what they've done, it's a really good battle to have in the ALCS," Armstrong said. "We're thankful to be here. So are they. At the end of the day, I hope we come out on top." Martinez pitched brilliantly against the Guardians during the 2026 regular season, winning both starts while allowing seven hits and one walk over 13 scoreless innings. He added nine strikeouts as Cleveland posted a .159/.178/.182 slash line against him. The 36-year-old Miami native pitched 3 2/3 innings and gave up two runs against the New York Yankees when he started Game 3 of the AL Division Series. Martinez went 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA in 31 regular-season starts this year, but Cash made him a relief option earlier in the ALCS. "The first game, I sat in the bullpen and didn't really like it," Martinez said, chuckling. "I was in the dugout with cleats on the second game. Whatever the team needs, I'm up for it. That's got to be my mentality for the rest of the year." Martinez is 3-2 with a 4.39 ERA in eight career appearances (four starts) against the Guardians. He has pitched in Cleveland twice (one start), throwing nine scoreless innings with five strikeouts while compiling a 1-0 record. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: イエメン・アデン空港にミサイル、サウジ向け弾道弾は迎撃
item.description: [１７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[１７日 ロイター] - イエメンのアデン国際空港に１６日、ミサイルが着弾した。一方、サウジアラビア主導の連合軍は、紅海沿岸の都市ヤンブーに向かっていた弾道ミサイルを迎撃したと発表した。

連合軍はさらに紅海上空で巡航ミサイル２発、サウジ南部とリヤド地方で無人機（ドローン）３機を破壊したと発表した。攻撃主体は明らかにしなかった。

イエメン南部アデンの治安当局によると、空港の敷地内にミサイル２発が着弾した。死傷者は報告されていない。当局は親イラン武装組織フーシ派による攻撃だと主張し、同空港への攻撃は１週間足らずで２回目だと説明した。

ヤンブーはサウジの重要な石油輸出拠点で、同国はここから紅海経由で原油を国際市場に送ることで、ホルムズ海峡を迂回できる。

サウジの民間防衛当局は１７日未明、イエメン国境に近い南西部アブハに警報を出し、その後解除した。これに先立ち、ジザン地方と南西部のハミースムシャイトにも警報を出していた。

フーシ派系メディアは１７日未明、イエメン北西部サアダの東で攻撃があったと報じた。サウジ主導の連合軍は、同地域で弾道ミサイル発射装置２基を破壊したと発表した。

item.title: Boca Juniors remonta ante Talleres y toma el liderato en la tabla anual del fútbol argentino
item.description: Boca Juniors se colocó en la cima de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino al remontar un marcador adverso y vencer el viernes 2-1 como local a Talleres de Córdoba en la decimotercera jornada del Torneo Clausura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boca Juniors se colocó en la cima de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino al remontar un marcador adverso y vencer el viernes 2-1 como local a Talleres de Córdoba en la decimotercera jornada del Torneo Clausura. Con este resultado, Boca llegó a 54 puntos en la sumatoria general que también otorga un título de campeón al final de la temporada. Independiente Rivadavia y Argentinos Juniors lo siguen con 52 y 51 unidades, respectivamente. "Siempre es lindo marcar con esta camiseta. Estamos muy contentos por el triunfo del equipo. Sabíamos que hoy teníamos que ganar para quedar arriba en la tabla", dijo el uruguayo Miguel Merentiel a la televisión local. En el partido disputado en el estadio La Bombonera, Talleres abrió el marcador a los 11 minutos con un remate de larga distancia de Matías Galarza que sorprendió al arquero colombiano Álvaro Montero. Merentiel anotó el empate para Boca a los 18 minutos con una definición precisa tras una asistencia de Lautaro Blanco. El segundo gol de Boca llegó a los 49 minutos por intermedio del joven Leonel Flores luego de una gran jugada individual y un remate cruzado. "Nos vamos con sensaciones tristes, porque no conseguimos el resultado que vinimos a buscar, pero hicimos un buen partido frente a un rival de mucha jerarquía", indicó Galarza tras la derrota. Por su parte, Instituto de Córdoba mantuvo el liderato de la Zona A al vencer 1-0 de visitante a Defensa y Justicia con un gol de Jeremías Lázaro a los 23 minutos. Instituto llegó a 29 puntos en la tabla de posiciones, cinco por encima de Defensa y Justicia y Boca Juniors. La jornada comenzó el jueves con el triunfo 2-1 de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata sobre Huracán.

item.title: Striking unions at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine reach preliminary deal, ending strike
item.description: Workers from two striking unions at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine in Chile reached a preliminary agreement on a new collective contract, ending a strike that has lasted more than a week at the mine, the unions said late on Friday in a statement sent to its members.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Workers from two striking unions at Antofagasta's (ANTO.L) Centinela copper mine in Chile reached a preliminary agreement on a new collective contract, ending a strike that has lasted more than a week at the mine, the unions said late on Friday in a statement sent to its members. The unions called a meeting on Friday night to present the agreement to members and a vote to ratify it will be held on Saturday. The more than 700 members of Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions [USN:L1N45T0DW TEXT:"began the strike"] on October 7 after contract talks failed. They had demanded that workers have the same benefits regardless of the union they belong to. The unions returned to the negotiating table this week to find a resolution to the conflict. Three striking workers had also been on a hunger strike since October 9 to pressure the parties into reaching a solution to the stalled talks. Antofagasta said it had presented the striking unions with new proposals covering key issues and offering a significant improvement in economic terms. The strike at Centinela, along with the [USN:L1N4600CR TEXT:"threat of a strike"] at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile, has been supporting global copper prices amid fears that it would be difficult to boost supply to meet projected future demand. Antofagasta said this week it has managed to [USN:S0N44M02N TEXT:"maintain production"] at normal levels, avoiding the negative effects of the work stoppage. In 2025, Centinela produced 240,400 metric tons of copper.

item.title: Trabajadores de mina chilena Centinela logran preacuerdo con Antofagasta para nuevo contrato y terminar huelga: sindicato
item.description: Los trabajadores de dos sindicatos en huelga de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela lograron un preacuerdo con Antofagasta Minerals para un nuevo contrato colectivo, lo que permitiría terminar la paralización de más de una semana, dijeron el viernes los gremios en un informativo enviado a sus socios.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los trabajadores de dos sindicatos en huelga de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela lograron un preacuerdo con Antofagasta Minerals para un nuevo contrato colectivo, lo que permitiría terminar la paralización de más de una semana, dijeron el viernes los gremios en un informativo enviado a sus socios. Los sindicatos Distrito Centinela y Minera Esperanza convocaron a una asamblea la noche del viernes para presentar el acuerdo, que será sometido a un voto de ratificación por los socios el sábado. Los más de 700 agremiados iniciaron la detención el 7 de octubre tras fracasar el diálogo contractual, donde pedían que los trabajadores tengan los mismos beneficios independiente del sindicato al pertenezcan. Pero esta semana volvieron a la mesa de diálogo en un intento por encontrar una salida al conflicto. En tanto, tres trabajadores mantenían una huelga de hambre en un intento por presionar una solución a las estancadas conversaciones entre las partes. Antofagasta afirmó en la semana que ha logrado sostener su producción en niveles normales lo que evitado los efectos negativos de la paralización. En 2025, Centinela produjo 240.400 toneladas de cobre. Además argumentó que durante esta semana había presentado nuevas propuestas con materias relevantes y una mejora significativa en las condiciones económicas. La huelga en Centinela, además del riesgo finalmente no consumado de paralización de supervisores en Escondida, de BHP, ha estado apoyando los precios globales del cobre en medio de los temores sobre la dificultad de impulsar la oferta para abastecer el consumo estimado hacia adelante.

item.title: Beijing Seeks Tighter Grip on AI Exports Amid U.S. Rivalry
item.description: By Eduardo Baptista China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on Friday, including those involving models, agents, and computing clusters, in a move to limit transfers of tools it views as vital to national security and to counter geopolitical competition with Washington. The proposals …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Eduardo Baptista

China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on Friday, including those involving models, agents, and computing clusters, in a move to limit transfers of tools it views as vital to national security and to counter geopolitical competition with Washington.

The proposals cover overseas deployment of AI models containing restricted technology, but exclude access through application programming interfaces (APIs), websites, apps and software-as-a-service platforms, China’s commerce ministry said.

The distinction could let Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Alibaba keep expanding internationally while giving Beijing greater oversight of transfers of sensitive AI technology abroad.

Chinese AI models have gained ground abroad thanks to lower prices and improving capabilities since DeepSeek’s R1 model emerged early last year, raising the stakes for Beijing as it decides how tightly to guard the sector.

Reuters reported in July that Chinese authorities had discussed with major technology companies, including Alibaba, ByteDance and Z.AI, potentially restricting overseas access to China’s most advanced AI models, including unreleased ones.

Preventing AI From Harming National Security

Frontier models like Anthropic’s Mythos have shown AI’s potential to turbocharge cyberattacks, worrying Beijing and prompting Chinese companies to develop their own versions.

Washington’s export controls on China’s access to cutting-edge American AI chips needed to train frontier models have so far helped keep US firms Anthropic and OpenAI in the lead, though Chinese rivals are finding workarounds to narrow the gap.

While both countries strive to lead in AI, some bilateral efforts are underway to address the existential risks the technology poses. The two powers have agreed to keep humans in control of nuclear-weapons decisions and last month set up a dialogue and an incident-communications channel for advanced AI.

The commerce ministry said on Friday the controls were partly intended to prevent misuse of AI technologies, including systems capable of autonomously generating and modifying malicious software that could threaten critical infrastructure and national security.

It said most AI technologies would remain freely exportable, with simplified licensing for open-source technology exports and Chinese companies operating their own computing centers overseas. Technology already in the public domain through open-source releases or academic papers would be outside the proposed controls.

Broader Revision

The proposals form part of a broader revision of China’s technology export catalog, covering 40 technologies across AI, biotechnology and solar power.

The proposals also include a ban on transferring intellectual property ownership for some novel cell and gene therapies and small interfering RNA (siRNA) technologies.

Exporters must register certain overseas technology transfers from Friday, pending final rules after public consultation on the proposals closes November 15.
item.wire:summarySource: The China-Global South Project source metadata
